title: Prove all-field negative correlation for corank-one pairs (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped algebraic proof with finite corroboration, answering Open next question 1 of #4747. For two full-guard corank-one requests with orthogonal rank-one kernels and complete uniformly weighted GL_m(F_q) headers:

```diff
- Strict negative correlation proved at q=2 and q=3
+ Pr(A and B) < (1-q^(-m)) Pr(A)Pr(B), every finite field q and m>=2
```

The written proof cites #4747's joint law and #4227's marginal law, then uses `beta-gamma=q(q-1)>0` and `q beta-alpha=(q-1)(2q^2-2q+1)>0`. The latter gives the power comparison in every dimension. There is no finite cutoff or unrun tail. This is a new consequence of those theorems, rather than an independent audit of them. The binary and ternary predecessor results retain #4261/#4273's credit.

Only `research/corankone-pair-correlation/` is added. This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Cinna Davis supplied the BIT request context; source527, commdata2338 and Jose Manuel retain the normalizer lineage credit. No new kappa or selected-frontier change is claimed.

[Advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19131124). Base `b58ad9ef4d4e861b0eaa5dba41742bdc072dca51`, priority revision 7. The explicit scope change and overlap coverage are in TASK.json. Canonical main advanced to `1f87c3578ae546c8f903f7f4d83dc2e2fb99650b` at the submission refresh; the entry guidance, catalogue, family status and selected record were unchanged. Main and merged searches were repeated against that refreshed base.

## Evidence

- Before: #4747 left all-field negative correlation open. After: PROOF.md proves the quantitative relative deficit `1-J/p^2 > q^(-m)` using two positive polynomial factorizations.
- All **4,032** exact parameter comparisons pass for integers `2<=q<=64`, `2<=m<=65`. Non-prime-power q test the algebra only. An independent polynomial coefficient multiplication checks the central factorization.
- Nine controls cover independence, two correction-term mutations, a literal singleton-header restriction and five invalid finite replay inputs. A separate reversed-sign polynomial control rejects its mutant. The exact fixture ratios are `28/243`, `24/49`, `40/49` at `(q,m)=(2,3),(3,2),(5,2)`.
- Both registered commands pass locally, with warnings as errors and explicit checks active under optimized Python. Their measured local durations were **0.081 s** and **0.085 s**. The registered timeout is 120 s. Ruff E/F/B/UP and AST function-size checks pass; the longest function is 28 lines.
- Exact committed-byte/source-history preflight, official export integrity and both Git-free exported replays pass at `c16deb7f640e2833097d8fd67e83ec179156aba5`. Exported replays also pass with `PATH=/nonexistent` and leave all seven exported files unchanged. Generated stdout JSON binds all six package files by SHA256; no receipt is handwritten or committed.
- The selected source-binding orientation prints `PASS_RESEARCH_BASELINE_BINDINGS_ONLY`. This is metadata orientation only; the selected construction was not replayed.

From the repository root, using CPython 3.12 in place of this exact local interpreter if needed:

Expected markers: `PASS_CORANKONE_PAIR_CORRELATION`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`, `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`. The verifier is standard-library-only and writes nothing. Full Git history is needed for the source-history preflight.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The theorem uses #4747's pending joint-law result at exact head `f51dcebce79b8b8958427a9a9b7bc8feca352c9d` as a mathematical dependency. SOURCES.json records its immutable external citation and hash separately from machine-validated retained-main provenance. No predecessor code or proof is imported at runtime; the generic metadata framework does not validate the external bibliography entry.

Only two orthogonal rank-one kernels and the complete uniform GL domain are covered. A literal singleton-header example shows that restricted catalogues can violate the bound. Nonorthogonal kernels, three or more requests and negative association are outside scope.

No actual producer or paid selection, emission, dispatch, restoration, stock, precision or complete physical caller is supplied. Those costs remain unknown. No supplier admission or complete multiplication theorem follows. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. Lean, Docker and selected cold replay were not run. All registered local package checks ran. CPython dynamic allocation is explicitly bounded by the fixed finite replay domain.

## Related open work

- #4747 supplies the exact two-request all-field joint law and poses the question answered here. At q=5,m=2, the checked values J=2/5 and p=7/10 give J/p^2=40/49, agreeing with its published joint fraction.
- #4619 classifies five-request binary threshold decompositions in the same orthogonal-kernel family. Its k=5 orbit and header counts do not overlap this two-request theorem, so no common numerical count is asserted.

- #4769, head `e7e3b621de13975ab493cada045b12d72a2e2b14`, gives an all-field one-way-coupled corank-one header law. Its UV nonzero, VU=0 contract differs from this PR's UV=VU=0. At q=3,m=3, the common marginal is **49/117**; exact evaluation gives this PR's orthogonal J=14/117=42/351 and its one-way J=53/351, agreeing with #4769's stated comparison. These are different joint events, not conflicting counts.

The current titles and bodies of #4747/#4619 and merged #4598/#4599/#4605/#4606/#4607 were read. Merged #4605's overlapping k=2,m=3 count agrees numerically: J=1/84, p=9/28, J/p^2=28/243, and 168J=2 complete headers. The four- and five-request counts of the other predecessors are different quantities and were not recounted.


Before DONE, this account's open PRs created since the CLAIM at **2026-10-22 19:18:40 UTC** were refreshed. Ten open PRs were returned, including this PR. #4769 is the new related header result addressed above. #4761 concerns binary chain retiming; #4763/#4764/#4766/#4770/#4772/#4773 concern right-vector target costs, counts or obstructions; #4771 concerns prescribed scalar-pivot Schur dimensions. None of those other eight studies this pair-header probability. No conflicting overlapping number was found.

## Open next questions

1. Does negative association hold for disjoint groups in larger orthogonal-kernel families? Start by comparing the binary three-event law in #4275 with the pair law times one marginal. Pairwise negative correlation alone does not settle it.
2. Can a real odd-field producer use a fully charged shared-header caller? Pin its kernel lines and actual header domain before charging selection, emission, dispatch, restoration and stock.
